source: Copy of 2-6Q_Lines-exponents-radicals version (b) P3 (early finishers version a). Original (version b). 25^(x+1) = 125^(2x-3); (2 + sqrt3)(a + b sqrt3) = 12 + 7 sqrt3; 3(9^x) - 82(3^x) + 27 = 0 with u = 3^x.

parts.label: a
parts.notes: M1 for writing both sides as powers of 5. A1 for 2x + 2 = 6x - 9 (or equivalent). A1 for 11/4. A GDC answer with no working earns M0A0A1. Wrong methods: a bracket not multiplied out (2x + 1 = 6x - 9 gives 5/2; 2x + 2 = 6x - 3 gives 5/4): M1A0A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find integers a, b with (2 + sqrt3)(a + b sqrt3) = 12 + 7 sqrt3.
parts.notes: M1 for expanding the product and comparing rational and surd parts, or for dividing by 2 + sqrt3 and multiplying by the conjugate 2 - sqrt3. A1 for the pair of equations 2a + 3b = 12, a + 2b = 7, or for the rationalized form (24 - 12 sqrt3 + 14 sqrt3 - 21)/1. A1 for a = 3, b = 2. Trial with the expansion (2 + sqrt3)(3 + 2 sqrt3) = 12 + 7 sqrt3 shown as a check earns M1A1A1. A bare answer earns M0A0A1.

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept x = -1, x = 3 in any order.
parts.notes: M1 for the quadratic 3u^2 - 82u + 27 = 0 (using 9^x = u^2). A1 for u = 1/3, A1 for u = 27 (by factorizing, formula or GDC). A1 for x = -1. A1 for x = 3. Stopping at u = 1/3, 27 earns M1A1A1A0A0. Wrong method: reading 3^x as 3x gives x = 1/9, 9: A0A0 for those values.

source: Copy of 2-6Q_Lines-exponents-radicals version (b) P4 (early finishers version a). Original (unit 1 material, version b). Arithmetic u_1 = 7, d = 3; geometric v_1 = 2, r = 1.5; v_n > u_n first at n = 8; geometric sum > arithmetic sum first at n = 10.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Write down expressions for u_n (u_1 = 7, d = 3) and v_n (v_1 = 2, r = 1.5).
parts.tolerance: Accept any equivalent expressions, e.g. u_n = 3n + 4.
parts.notes: A1 for u_n, A1 for v_n, independently.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the least n for which v_n > u_n.
parts.notes: M1 for the inequality with their expressions, or a GDC table or graph of both sequences. A1 for the values on both sides of the change (n = 7 and n = 8), or a marked intersection near 7.6. A1 for n = 8. A final answer of 7.6 earns the final A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from (a): v_n = 2(1.5)^n gives n = 7, which earns full FT marks if consistent.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the least n for which the geometric sum of n terms exceeds the arithmetic sum of n terms.
parts.notes: M1 for both sum formulas with their values (or a GDC table of both sums). A1 for the sums on both sides of the change (n = 9 and n = 10). A1 for n = 10. Wrong method: comparing terms instead of sums gives n = 8: M0A0A0.
